name: eyelid-shaw-2010
label: Eyelid pressure on the ocular surface (primary gaze, static)
upperPressureCitation: Shaw AJ, Collins MJ, Davis BA, Carney LG, Eyelid pressure and contact with the ocular surface, Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2010 (PubMed 19834035): 8.0 +/- 3.4 mmHg, derived with the pressure-sensitive paper imprint widths (11 young adults), the authors' preferred estimate; the whole-cell estimate was 3.8 +/- 0.7 and the Marx's-line estimate 55 +/- 26 mmHg (excerpt).
upperContactCitation: Shaw et al. 2010: mean contact width of the upper lid margin band on the ocular surface 0.60 +/- 0.16 mm from the imprints (excerpt). Used as the vertical extent of the pressure band.
lowerCitation: assumption: no excerpt gave a lower-lid pressure or contact width (Shaw's 2009 QUT thesis measured lower-lid effects on topography); the upper-lid values are used.
apertureCitation: Mean of three excerpted adult population means of vertical palpebral fissure height: 10.3-10.4 mm (Turkish young adults), 9.35-9.41 mm (Serbian young adults), 10.6 mm (mixed sample, mean age 36.5). The lid bands are placed symmetrically about the corneal center (approximation; in primary gaze the lower lid sits near the inferior limbus and the upper lid covers 1-2 mm of the superior cornea).
